name: Learn a headstand
blurb: A tripod of head and hands makes this far easier than a handstand, but only if you build the neck strength gradually and put the weight in the right place.
gear: A folded blanket or a mat
A wall for the first attempts
steps: Set the tripod: forearms down, hands cupping the back of the head, crown on the floor, forming a triangle. Roughly 70% of the weight goes through the arms, not the head.
Walk your feet in until your hips stack over your shoulders.
Lift one knee to your chest, then the other, and hold tucked for 30 seconds.
Extend the legs slowly to vertical, keeping the ribs down.
Build up to a minute, then move away from the wall.
Learn to exit by tucking back down under control rather than falling out.
tips: Neck pain means too much weight on your head. Press harder through the forearms.
Do not attempt this with a neck injury, and build up over weeks rather than days.
proof: One minute freestanding with straight legs and no wall.
